question: What is an LLM's context window, and what happens when the input is longer than it?

outcomes.answer:
An LLM's context window is the maximum number of tokens a model can process in a single request, encompassing the prompt, any provided input documents, and the tokens generated in the model's response [S1].

When an input exceeds this limit, most APIs will reject the request with a context-length error [S2]. Alternatively, some client libraries may automatically truncate either the oldest or the last part of the input, causing the model to never process that specific text [S2]. To manage inputs that exceed the context window, common strategies include splitting the text into chunks, summarizing sections before processing, or using retrieval methods to include only the passages relevant to the query [S3].
